answers: Who keeps it: Training input / RLaaS / post-training / continual-learning infra
band_rationale: Normal = an hour or more between learning from use and serving the update, the pace of a retrain-and-redeploy pipeline; fast = a quarter of an hour or less, updates flowing near-continuously. Every row is a vendor describing itself (tier 7), so the status caps at emerging.
counterevidence: Vendors describe their fastest path, not their typical one; an hour-long pipeline can still ship rarely, and a fast one can ship small, low-value updates.

crosswalk.note: Expert data, RL environments and continual-learning infra are the deployment→invention channel; lab recoupment ⇄ capex-to-revenue.

definition: The shortest interval, among vendors describing it in production, between a model update learned from live use and that update serving traffic. Derived metric cl_refresh_cadence_hours from rows citing each vendor's own description.
name: Fastest production refresh of a continually updated model (hours)
stale_reason: Event-driven: a vendor describes its pipeline once; a quiet quarter means nothing new was described.

status_events.author: claude
status_events.reason: First reading: Trajectory's pipeline, as Baseten describes it, puts a freshly trained adapter behind a live endpoint in roughly an hour, on the edge of the normal band. The only source is the vendor's own description (tier 7), so the status caps at emerging.

timing_rationale: Leading: the refresh interval shortens before continual learning shows in products or capability.
tracker_interpretation: One vendor's pipeline sets the reading; the refresh is a retrained adapter, not learning inside the model between sessions.
why_it_matters: How quickly deployment feeds back into the model is the return arrow's speed; a refresh measured in minutes is continual learning in all but name.
